documents.deep: 01 基本信息 标题 ：Cerberus: bidirectional state space blocks improve accuracy and efficiency of regulatory sequence models 作者 ：Kelley DR; Yuan H; Huang X; Linder J 单位 ：未提供 期刊/平台 ：bioRxiv（预印本） 年份 ：2026-10-09 论文类型 ：预印本（方法学 + 基准评测） 领域 ：调控基因组学 / 序列-功能预测 / 深度学习架构 关键词 ：state space models, Mamba-2, regulatory genomics, variant effect prediction, Borzoi, Cerberus DOI/arXiv ：10.64898/2026.10.02.756377 代码 ：作者声明发布模型、训练数据、训练与评估代码、基准集（具体链接未提供） 数据 ：GTEx v11 fine-mapped eQTL/sQTL/paQTL；augmented track collection（具体构成未提供） 阅读日期 ：未提供 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「序列-功能预测 × 深度学习架构」方向，核心贡献是用双向状态空间模型（Mamba-2）替代 transformer 自注意力，在长序列调控建模中同时提升效率与精度。对三维基因组/染色质组织 × AI 方向而言，其可迁移点在于：长程相互作用建模的线性复杂度架构、多尺度交互范围的可解释性分析（block depth vs. interaction range）、以及变异效应预测的基准评测协议。 02 一句话总结 本文用基于 Mamba-2 的双向状态空间块（Hydra）替换 Borzoi 的 transformer 块，在保持训练数据与其余架构不变的前提下，以 5.7 倍更快的速度、32 bp 分辨率（去掉 U-net decoder）获得更准确的调控活性预测与 eQTL 分类，并扩展为 786 kb 输入的八模型集成 Cerberus，在 GTEx v11 三类 QTL 基准上优于 Borzoi。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：在参考基因组提供的唯一训练序列有限、新实验只增加标签不增加序列的条件下，如何设计序列-功能模型的架构，使其从有限的序列多样性中学到更多、更准的调控规则？ 为什么重要 ：长程调控相互作用（enhancer-promoter、CTCF 边界等）对基因表达预测和变异效应解释至关重要；现有 SOTA 模型（Borzoi）依赖 self-attention，其计算成本随序列长度二次增长，限制了分辨率和可处理的输入长度。 现有方法为何不足 ：transformer 的 self-attention 在长序列上计算昂贵，迫使 Borzoi 使用较低分辨率（如 128 bp）和 U-net decoder 来折中；这限制了模型对精细调控元件的分辨能力，也限制了从有限序列中提取信息的效率。 精确研究问题 ：Can a bidirectional state space block (Mamba-2-based) replace transformer blocks in a regulatory sequence model to improve both accuracy and efficiency on held-out sequence prediction and variant effect classification, while enabling higher input resolution? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络基于本文框架，未经外部系统核验。 阶段 代表方法 优点 局限 本文位置 第一代：卷积模型 DeepSEA, Basenji 可处理局部 motif；计算高效 感受野有限，难以捕捉长程调控 本文保留卷积前端作为局部特征提取 第二代：transformer 长程模型 Enformer, Borzoi self-attention 可建模长程交互；borzoi 在变异效应预测上 SOTA 二次复杂度限制分辨率与输入长度；训练数据有限时参数效率低 本文用 SSM 替代 transformer 作为长程块 第三代：状态空间模型 Mamba, Mamba-2 线性复杂度；选择性扫描可建模长程依赖 单向扫描可能遗漏双向上下文 本文提出 Hydra（双向 SSM 块），在调控序列上验证优于 transformer 集成与扩展 AlphaGenome 等 更大模型、更多数据 计算成本高；未必在有限数据下最优 Cerberus 在 786 kb 输入上集成 8 模型，在 QTL 基准上部分超越 AlphaGenome 05 核心痛点 痛点 表现 成因或作者解释 文中证据 训练序列有限 参考基因组提供唯一序列集合；新实验只加标签不加序列 基因组序列是固定的，无法像 NLP/CV 那样无限扩充数据 引言部分（未提供具体节号） Transformer 计算成本高 长序列上 self-attention 二次复杂度；Borzoi 被迫用低分辨率（128 bp） 自注意力对每对 token 计算交互，长度平方增长 作者在引言/方法中对比 Hydra 与 transformer 速度（5.7× faster on 8,192 tokens） 分辨率受限 低分辨率（如 128 bp）无法分辨精细调控元件 计算预算限制下需在分辨率与输入长度间取舍 作者用 32 bp 分辨率运行 Hydra 块并去掉 U-net decoder 有限数据下参数效率低 transformer 在大规模预训练数据上表现好，但在基因组有限数据下可能过拟合或欠拟合 自注意力参数多，需要更多数据拟合 作者在固定训练数据下对比 Hydra 与 transformer 块，Hydra 更优 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 ：将 Borzoi 的 transformer 块替换为 Hydra——一种基于 Mamba-2 的双向状态空间块；在固定其余架构与训练数据的条件下对比；随后将 Hydra 模型扩展到 32 bp 分辨率、去掉 U-net decoder，并集成 8 个模型形成 Cerberus。 2) 核心洞察 ：双向状态空间模型（SSM）在线性复杂度下能有效建模长程依赖，且其选择性扫描机制天然适合调控基因组学中「少数关键远距离元件决定表达」的稀疏交互模式。双向性弥补了单向 Mamba 的上下文缺失，使模型在有限数据下比 transformer 更高效地利用序列信息。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ：在数据量有限但序列长度极长的领域（如三维基因组中 Hi-C 接触图预测、enhancer-promoter 交互预测），二次复杂度的注意力机制可能不是最优选择；线性复杂度的 SSM 架构配合双向扫描，可能在精度与效率上同时超越 transformer。此外，「固定数据与其余架构、只换核心块」的消融对比设计，是评估架构贡献的干净范式。 07 方法总览 输入 ：DNA 序列（Cerberus 为 786 kb 输入窗口；Hydra 对比实验为 8,192 token 输入） 输出 ：binned coverage 预测（调控活性）；变异效应预测（eQTL/sQTL/paQTL 分类与效应量估计） 模块 ： 1. 卷积前端（保留 Borzoi 设计）：局部 motif 特征提取 2. Hydra 块（替代 transformer）：双向 Mamba-2 状态空间块，线性复杂度 3. 输出头：binned coverage 预测头（去掉 U-net decoder，直接以 32 bp 分辨率输出） 4. 集成：8 个模型组成 Cerberus 集成 训练 ：在 augmented track collection 上训练（具体构成未提供）；对比实验固定训练数据与其余架构 任务范围 ：本文结论限于调控序列建模（binned coverage 预测）与 QTL 变异效应预测（eQTL/sQTL/paQTL），不涉及三维基因组结构预测或染色质构象建模。 oracle/真值输入 ：fine-mapped QTL 来自 GTEx v11，属于实验推导的因果变异集合；负样本匹配策略（allele frequency、gene expression、positional annotations）旨在减少混淆，但无法完全排除残余混淆。 端到端状态 ：Cerberus 是端到端训练的序列-功能模型，但变异效应预测依赖 in silico 突变扫描（从 coverage 预测推导），属于间接预测。 算力成本 ：未提供训练/推理的具体算力需求；仅报告 Hydra 比 transformer 快 5.7 倍（8,192 token 输入）。 历史数据依赖 ：训练数据为 augmented track collection，具体构成未提供；无法评估数据偏差。 模型依赖 ：结论基于 Mamba-2 双向 SSM；不保证其他 SSM 变体（如 S4、Hyena）有同样效果。 最难情形 ：编码区与 <3 kb 变异上落后于 AlphaGenome；短距离调控变异的预测仍是短板。 不确定性 ：未提供置信区间、显著性检验或跨组织方差分析；预印本未经同行评审。 有边界的复述 ：在固定训练数据与其余架构的条件下，双向 SSM 块（Hydra）在 8,192 token 输入上比 transformer 快 5.7 倍且 eQTL 分类更准；扩展到 32 bp 分辨率并集成为 Cerberus 后，在 GTEx v11 三类 QTL 基准上整体优于 Borzoi，但在短距离/编码区变异上不如 AlphaGenome。 12 作者自认局限 交互预测通常需要处理百万级 bin 的序列或矩阵，transformer 的二次复杂度是瓶颈；SSM 的线性复杂度天然适合超长序列建模。迁移路径：将 Hydra 块用于序列-接触图联合预测模型，或用于处理 1 Mb+ 的调控序列窗口。 「固定其余架构与数据、只换核心块」的消融范式 ：本文最干净的贡献是严格隔离了架构变量的影响。 可迁移到三维基因组 ：在比较不同长程建模架构（transformer vs. SSM vs. Hyena）对 Hi-C 预测的影响时，应采用同样的消融设计，避免数据增强或 decoder 改动混淆归因。 高分辨率直接输出替代 U-net decoder ：32 bp 分辨率直接输出（去掉 U-net）在更小模型下获得更高精度。 可迁移到三维基因组 ：Hi-C 预测中常使用 U-net 式 decoder 从低分辨率恢复高分辨率接触图；本文证据提示，若骨干网络足够高效，直接高分辨率输出可能更优。 分层交互范围分析（block depth vs. interaction range） ：从第 1 块 0.9 kb 到第 7 块 79 kb 的中位交互半衰期，且深层锚定 CTCF。 可迁移到三维基因组 ：这一分析范式可直接用于检查模型是否学习到多尺度染色质组织（TAD、compartment、loop）；若模型深层交互锚定 CTCF/cohesin motif，则提示模型隐式学习了 3D 基因组结构特征。 负样本匹配协议 ：匹配 allele frequency、gene expression、positional annotations 的 QTL 基准设计。 可迁移到三维基因组 ：在评估 (abstract-level detail provided) Assessment boundary Claims and evidence as presented in the supplied text only Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce Cerberus, an ensemble of eight sequence-to-function models built on Hydra, a bidirectional state space block derived from Mamba-2. They claim Hydra blocks are faster than Borzoi's transformer blocks, that models using Hydra predict regulatory activity and classify eQTLs more accurately, that running at 32 bp resolution allows removal of the U-net decoder, and that Cerberus outperforms Borzoi on eQTL, sQTL, and paQTL benchmarks while trading leads with AlphaGenome. They also claim interpretable interaction ranges that grow with block depth. Visible evidence base Abstract text only. No figures, tables, methods, or supplementary materials provided. Missing materials affecting confidence All figures, tables, methods details, benchmark definitions, model architecture specifications, training procedures, statistical tests, and code availability verification. The provided text is an abstract-level summary without quantitative uncertainty estimates or methodological detail. Reviewer Overall assessment The manuscript addresses a timely and important problem in regulatory genomics: improving sequence-to-function model accuracy and efficiency under the constraint of limited unique training sequences. The core architectural contribution, replacing self-attention with bidirectional state space blocks, is plausible and potentially impactful. However, the supplied material is an abstract-level summary that does not permit verification of the central claims. Key methodological details, statistical rigor, and benchmark construction are not assessable from the provided text. The claims are promising but currently not established from the evidence provided. Who would be interested in the results, and why Computational biologists developing sequence-to-function models, researchers studying regulatory genomics and variant effect prediction, and methodologists interested in efficient long-range sequence modeling. The efficiency gains and accuracy improvements over Borzoi would be of practical interest to the genomics community, and the architectural comparison between attention and state space models has broader relevance to machine learning researchers working on biological sequences. Major strengths The problem framing is well motivated, emphasizing the fixed reference genome constraint and the value of architectures that learn more from limited sequence diversity. The architectural comparison is clean in principle, holding other components fixed. The efficiency gain of 5.7-fold is substantial and practically meaningful. The evaluation across multiple variant classes (eQTL, sQTL, paQTL) with matched negatives addresses known confounding issues. The release of models, code, and benchmarks is commendable for reproducibility. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Hydra blocks ran 5.7-fold faster on 8,192-token inputs, and models built on them predicted binned coverage on held-out sequences and classified fine-mapped eQTLs more accurately." Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The speed and accuracy claims are presented without any experimental detail. No information is given about hardware, batch size, sequence length distribution, or the specific metrics and statistical tests used to establish that the accuracy differences are significant. The eQTL classification improvement is not quantified in this sentence, and no confidence intervals or significance tests are reported anywhere in the supplied text. Why it matters Without knowing the variance across replicates or the statistical significance of the accuracy differences, the reader cannot determine whether the reported improvements are robust or within noise. The 5.7-fold speedup claim requires specification of the exact comparison conditions to be meaningful. Resolution test Provide benchmark details including hardware specifications, timing methodology, number of replicates, and statistical significance tests (e.g., paired tests across validation folds or tissues) for all accuracy comparisons. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Cerberus is more accurate than Borzoi on all three phenotypes, 0.692 versus 0.668 mean eQTL AUPRC across 48 tissues, and estimates eQTL effect sizes better, 0.379 versus 0.321 Spearman rho." Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The headline performance numbers are reported as point estimates without any measure of uncertainty. For the eQTL AUPRC, the mean across 48 tissues is given, but no standard deviation, standard error, or per-tissue distribution is shown. The Spearman rho comparison similarly lacks confidence intervals. It is unclear whether these differences are statistically significant and whether they are consistent across tissues or driven by a subset. Why it matters In benchmark comparisons, point estimates without uncertainty can be misleading. The claim that Cerberus is "more accurate" on all three phenotypes requires evidence that the differences are not attributable to chance, particularly given the matched-negative design which may introduce subtle biases. Resolution test Report per-tissue results with measures of variance, perform paired statistical tests across tissues, and provide confidence intervals for all reported metrics. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Benchmark validity Claim pointer "We evaluated it on GTEx v11 fine-mapped eQTL, sQTL, and paQTL benchmarks with negatives matched on allele frequency, gene expression, and phenotype-specific positional annotations to reduce confounding by these properties." Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The negative matching strategy is described at a high level but without sufficient detail to assess its adequacy. Matching on allele frequency, gene expression, and positional annotations is sensible, but the exact matching procedure, the number of negatives per positive, the tolerance thresholds, and whether matching was performed separately for each phenotype are not specified. The statement "to reduce confounding" acknowledges the limitation but does not establish that confounding was adequately controlled. Why it matters The validity of the benchmark depends critically on the quality of negative sets. If matching is imperfect, the reported accuracy differences could reflect artifacts of the benchmark construction rather than genuine model performance. The comparison with AlphaGenome, which may use different benchmark construction, is particularly sensitive to this issue. Resolution Test Provide detailed description of the negative matching procedure, including exact matching criteria, quality checks, and sensitivity analyses demonstrating that results are robust to matching parameters. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Hydra's linear cost in sequence length let us run the blocks at 32 bp resolution and remove the U-net decoder, leaving a convolution-SSM model smaller and more accurate than the one it replaced." Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The claim that removing the U-net decoder and running at 32 bp resolution yields a model that is both smaller and more accurate is central to the architectural contribution, but no details are provided on model size, parameter counts, or the specific accuracy comparison supporting this claim. The interaction between resolution, decoder removal, and accuracy is not explained. Why it matters This claim justifies the architectural design choice. Without quantitative details on model size and the accuracy comparison, the reader cannot evaluate whether the trade-off is favorable or whether the comparison was fair (e.g., same training budget, same evaluation protocol). Resolution Test Report parameter counts for both architectures, describe the training setup, and provide the accuracy comparison with appropriate controls. Concern ID R1-M5 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Interpretability Claim pointer "Interpretation of the trained blocks shows interaction range growing with block depth, from a 0.9 kb median half-life in the first block to 79 kb in the seventh, and the deepest heads anchoring on promoters, enhancers, and CTCF peaks." Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The interpretability analysis is described in two sentences without any methodological detail. The "median half-life" metric is not defined, the method for measuring interaction range is not specified, and the claim about "deepest heads anchoring" on genomic features lacks quantitative support. It is unclear how these conclusions were derived and whether they are robust. Why it matters The interpretability results are presented as supporting evidence for the model's biological relevance. Without methodological detail, these claims cannot be evaluated or reproduced, and the reader cannot assess whether the interpretation is meaningful or an artifact of the analysis method. Resolution Test Provide the interpretation methodology, define all metrics, show the distribution of interaction ranges across blocks, and provide statistical support for the anchoring claims. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected Element Model naming Evidence pointer Location not provided Issue The relationship between Hydra, Cerberus, and the "convolution-SSM model" is not entirely clear. The text describes Hydra as a block type, then refers to a "convolution-SSM model" after removing the U-net, and finally introduces Cerberus as an ensemble. The hierarchy of these terms should be clarified. Required Correction Define each model name explicitly and describe the relationship between them (e.g., is Cerberus an ensemble of the convolution-SSM model trained on augmented data?). Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected Element Comparison with AlphaGenome Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The comparison with AlphaGenome is described only in terms of eQTL classification, with Cerberus ahead on variants 3 to 100 kb from the TSS and behind in coding sequence and within 3 kb. No quantitative results are given for this comparison. Required Correction Provide the quantitative results for the AlphaGenome comparison, including the specific metrics and the breakdown by distance-to-TSS categories. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Reproducibility Affected Element Data and code release Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The release of "the training data" is mentioned, but it is unclear what this includes given that the reference genome and GTEx data are public. The augmented track collection is mentioned but not described. Required Correction Specify what constitutes the released training data, describe the augmented track collection, and provide the repository URLs or accession numbers. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected Element "Trades leads" phrasing Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The phrase "trades leads" is informal and ambiguous. It is unclear whether this means the models are comparable overall with differences in specific regions, or whether there is a systematic tradeoff. Required Correction Replace with a precise description of the comparative performance, including overall metrics and the specific regions where each model performs better. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1, R1-M2, R1-M3, R1-M4, R1-M5. The supplied material is an abstract-level summary that does not provide the methodological detail, statistical rigor, or quantitative evidence needed to establish the central claims of the manuscript. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The application of bidirectional state space blocks to regulatory sequence modeling is a novel contribution that extends recent advances in efficient sequence modeling to genomics. The specific architectural choices and the systematic comparison with attention-based models are original. Scientific importance: The problem of improving sequence-to-function models under the constraint of limited training sequences is important for understanding gene regulation and interpreting genetic variants. The potential efficiency gains are practically significant. Interdisciplinary readership: The work bridges machine learning and genomics, and the results would be of interest to both communities. The efficiency and accuracy improvements are broadly relevant. Technical soundness: Not assessable from the supplied material. The claims require detailed methodological description and statistical validation that are not provided. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is generally accessible, but the technical claims (e.g., "bidirectional state space block," "median half-life") are not explained sufficiently for a broad audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The claims are promising and the direction is valuable, but the abstract-level material does not permit verification of the central results. A full manuscript with detailed methods, statistical analyses, and benchmark descriptions would be required to assess whether the claims hold. Risk / unsupported claims The 5.7-fold speedup claim is unsupported without hardware and benchmarking details. The accuracy improvements over Borzoi are unsupported without statistical significance testing and variance reporting. The claim that the convolution-SSM model is "smaller and more accurate" is unsupported without parameter counts and controlled comparisons. The interpretability results (interaction range growth, anchoring on genomic features) are unsupported without methodological detail. The benchmark construction and negative matching adequacy are not assessable from the supplied text. The comparison with AlphaGenome is not quantitatively supported. The claim that Cerberus "supports variant scoring and transfer learning" is stated without demonstration or evaluation.

Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, simulation parameters, or statistical analyses are available Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, simulation methodology details, parameter ranges, control simulations, and any statistical or error analysis Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible and potentially interesting computational study linking active loop extrusion to entanglement dilution and altered polymer conformations. However, the claims are broad and mechanistic, and the abstract alone provides insufficient quantitative detail to evaluate the robustness of the findings. The central assertions, particularly the nonmonotonic overlap parameter and the comparison between TAD and non-TAD systems, require direct evidence that is not visible here. The work may appeal to a specialized biophysics and chromatin biology audience, but its broader significance is not yet established from the supplied material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in computational polymer physics, chromatin organization, and gene regulation would be interested. The study addresses a fundamental question about how active processes alter entanglement and compaction in polymer melts, which is relevant to understanding chromosome architecture and the physical basis of TAD function. The potential link to cis-regulatory element efficiency could attract molecular biologists studying gene expression control. Major strengths The topic is timely and interdisciplinary, bridging polymer physics and chromatin biology. The use of hybrid molecular dynamics–Monte Carlo simulations is an appropriate approach for modeling active loop extrusion in entangled melts. The abstract identifies a clear and testable prediction, namely that active extrusion dilutes entanglements and reduces inter-TAD overlaps, which could have functional consequences. Evidence pointer Abstract only; location not provided Concern The abstract provides no quantitative data, such as actual overlap parameter values, contact probability curves, or comparisons across parameter ranges. The nonmonotonic behavior and the suppression of inter-TAD contacts are stated as findings, but no figures or statistical measures are referenced. Without these, the reader cannot assess the magnitude of the effects or whether they are robust to parameter variation. Why it matters The core novelty of the work appears to rest on these specific quantitative claims. If the nonmonotonicity is weak or parameter-dependent, the conclusion about entanglement dilution may not hold generally. Similarly, the claim about TAD suppression requires direct comparison data, which is absent. Cys563–KASH2 Cys6862）和 KASH β 链相互作用基序中的特定残基（KASH6875、KASH6877），并证明二者通过不同机制（分别影响力的大小与持续时间）调控跨核膜的力学传导，而非单一梯度式减损。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：LINC 复合物中哪些具体的分子接触（structural interactions）在承受机械负荷时维持力学连接？这些接触如何以不同的方式贡献于跨核膜的力传递？ 为什么重要 ：LINC 复合物是连接细胞骨架与核骨架的核心力学枢纽，调控核形态、染色质组织和下游信号传导。理解其力学传导的分子基础，是阐明力学信号如何影响染色质组织与核架构的前提，也与核纤层蛋白病（如 HGPS）的病理机制相关。 现有方法为何不足 ：此前研究多聚焦 LINC 复合物的整体结构与功能，缺乏对单个分子接触在负荷下力学贡献的定量解析。实验方法难以在原子尺度分辨特定残基在力传导中的角色。 精确研究问题 ：Can atomistic molecular dynamics simulations identify distinct molecular "force gates" within the SUN-KASH interface that differentially regulate the magnitude and duration of force transmission across the nuclear envelope? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：此脉络基于本文框架整理，未经外部系统核验，标注为「仅本文框架」。 阶段 代表性方法/认识 优点 局限 本文位置 结构解析阶段 晶体学/冷冻电镜解析 LINC 复合物结构 复合物的 SUN-KASH 界面进行原子级分子动力学模拟，通过引入靶向突变（破坏二硫键、破坏 β 链相互作用基序），比较突变体与野生型在力传导中的差异。 2) 核心洞察 ：LINC 复合物的力学传导不是由单一均匀的界面承担，而是由多个"力门"（force gates）——即特定的结构接触——分别调控力学传导的不同维度。二硫键（SUN2 Cys563–KASH2 Cys6862）主要调控力的大小（幅值），而 KASH β 链相互作用基序（KASH6875、KASH6877）主要调控力的持续时间与界面耦合。破坏不同力门产生不同的力学表型，而非简单的梯度式减损。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] ：在力学敏感蛋白界面中，"力传导"不是一个单一标量，而是由多个正交维度（幅值、持续时间、耦合方式）组成，每个维度可能由不同的分子接触独立调控。这一"力门"概念框架可能适用于其他承受机械负荷的蛋白界面（如黏着斑、离子通道等），也可为 AI 辅助的力学敏感界面预测提供新的标注维度——不仅要预测"是否传导力"，还要预测"传导哪种维度的力"。 07 方法总览 输入 ：LINC 复合物 SUN-KASH no figures, methods, or supplementary material were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors use atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to identify "force gates" in the LINC complex, specifically a disulfide bond (SUN2 Cys563 to KASH2 Cys6862) and residues within the KASH β strand interaction motif (KASH6875, KASH6877). They report that removing the disulfide reduces sustained and peak force transmission approximately twofold, while disrupting the β sheet network leaves peak force largely intact but alters interfacial coupling and load duration. They propose a "force gate" framework for mechanically loaded protein interfaces and suggest relevance to laminopathies, including HGPS, while noting that disease implications remain speculative. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no figures, tables, methods, simulation parameters, or statistical analyses were provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, simulation methodology, force measurement protocols, mutation validation, statistical analyses, and any experimental context Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially interesting computational framework for dissecting mechanical force transmission across the LINC complex. The central concept of distinct "force gates" contributing unequally to force transmission is plausible and could be of value to the mechanobiology community. However, the abstract alone provides insufficient evidence to evaluate the technical soundness of the simulations, the robustness of the findings, or the validity of the proposed framework. The claims are stated with confidence that exceeds what can be assessed from the provided material. The manuscript may merit consideration after full review of the methods and results, but the case is not established from the abstract alone. Who would be interested in the results, and why Mechanobiologists studying nuclear-cytoskeletal coupling, researchers working on LINC complex structure and function, computational biophysicists interested in force transmission at protein interfaces, and investigators studying laminopathies or nuclear mechanics. The framework could also interest those developing therapeutic strategies targeting mechanically regulated protein interfaces. Major strengths The abstract identifies a specific, mechanistically plausible hypothesis about distinct molecular contacts contributing differently to force transmission. The distinction between disulfide bond and β sheet network contributions is a clear and testable prediction. The authors appropriately acknowledge that disease implications are speculative and require experimental validation. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Technical soundness Claim pointer "Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we identify and characterize force gates within the LINC complex" Evidence pointer Methods not provided; location not provided Concern The abstract provides no information about simulation methodology, including force field parameters, simulation timescales, system size, equilibration protocols, or the number of independent replicates. Without this information, the technical validity of the simulations cannot be assessed. Atomistic MD simulations of protein complexes under mechanical load are highly sensitive to these parameters, and pulling rates or force application methods can dramatically influence results. Why it matters The central claims depend entirely on the reliability of the simulations. If the methodology is not sound, the identified "force gates" could be artifacts of the simulation setup rather than genuine mechanical elements. The approximately twofold reduction in force transmission upon disulfide removal is a quantitative claim that requires robust statistical treatment and appropriate sampling. Resolution test Provide full methods including force field, simulation box dimensions, water model, ion concentration, temperature and pressure coupling, equilibration time, production run length, number of replicates, pulling protocol (constant velocity vs constant force, pulling rate, spring constant), and convergence criteria. Show that results are reproducible across independent simulations and robust to parameter variation. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer "removing the disulfide reduces both sustained and peak force transmission approximately twofold, whereas disrupting the β sheet network leaves peak force largely intact while altering interfacial coupling and the duration over which load is borne" Evidence pointer Figures not provided; location not provided Concern The abstract reports quantitative differences between mutation conditions but provides no figures, error estimates, or statistical analyses. The claim of "approximately twofold" reduction and "largely intact" peak force cannot be evaluated without seeing the actual force traces, the variability across replicates, and the statistical significance of the differences. Why it matters The central conclusion that distinct molecular contacts contribute through "distinct routes rather than through a single graded loss of force" depends on the reliability of these quantitative comparisons. Without error bars, replicate numbers, or significance testing, the distinction between the two mutation effects could be within noise. Resolution test Provide force-time traces for wild-type and each mutant, with multiple replicates overlaid. Report mean and standard deviation or standard error for peak and sustained force values. Perform appropriate statistical tests (e.g., t-test or ANOVA) comparing conditions. Show that the differences are significant and reproducible. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Biological relevance Claim pointer "Such altered LINC mechanics may be relevant to laminopathies, including Hutchinson Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS), in which defective nuclear lamina compromises force transmission" Evidence pointer Location not provided Concern The connection between the simulated mutations and laminopathy pathology is not established. The abstract states that HGPS involves defective nuclear lamina, but does not explain how the specific mutations studied (SUN2 Cys563, KASH2 Cys6862, KASH6875, KASH6877) relate to any disease-associated variants or how altered LINC mechanics would contribute to laminopathy phenotypes. Why it matters The relevance to disease is stated as a potential implication, but the logical connection is not developed. If the authors intend to claim disease relevance, they need to show that the simulated mutations correspond to or mimic disease-associated changes, or that the force gate framework provides mechanistic insight into how lamina defects propagate through the LINC complex. Resolution test Either remove the disease relevance claim entirely, or provide evidence linking the specific simulated perturbations to known disease mechanisms. This could include sequence alignment with disease-associated variants, discussion of how lamina defects might alter forces experienced by the LINC complex, or experimental data on LINC function in disease models. It is unclear whether this refers to a threshold behavior, a structural element that modulates force transmission, or a regulatory mechanism. Required correction Provide an explicit definition of "force gate" early in the abstract, including the criteria by which a structural interaction qualifies as a force gate. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element Mutation description Evidence pointer Abstract text Issue The abstract mentions "targeted mutations" and specific residues (KASH6875, KASH6877) but does not state what these mutations are (e.g., alanine substitutions, deletions) or how they were designed. Required Correction Specify the exact mutations introduced and the rationale for choosing them. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Precision Affected element Quantitative claim Evidence pointer Abstract text Issue The phrase "approximately twofold" is vague. It is unclear whether this is 1.8-fold, 2.2-fold, or another value, and whether this applies to both sustained and peak force equally. Required Correction Report exact values with confidence intervals or standard deviations. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Scope Affected element Generalization claim Evidence pointer Abstract text Issue The abstract states that the "force gate framework may guide strategies to modulate interfaces that bear mechanical loads in other mechanically regulated proteins" without providing any evidence or reasoning for this generalization. Required Correction Either provide a brief rationale for why the framework should generalize, or soften the claim to reflect that this is a speculative extension. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 (simulation methodology not provided), R1-M2 (quantitative results without statistical support or figures) Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The concept of distinct "force gates" contributing unequally to force transmission is a potentially novel framing, but the abstract does not provide enough context to assess how this differs from existing models of LINC complex mechanics. Scientific importance: The LINC complex is a central mechanotransductive apparatus, and understanding how specific molecular contacts contribute to force transmission could be important. However, the disease relevance is not established, limiting the immediate impact. Interdisciplinary readership: The topic bridges mechanobiology, biophysics, and structural biology, which could attract a broad readership. However, the abstract assumes familiarity with LINC complex biology and MD simulation approaches. Technical soundness: Cannot be assessed from the abstract alone. The lack of methodological detail and statistical support is a significant concern. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is reasonably clear but uses domain-specific terminology (e.g., "KASH β strand interaction motif") without sufficient explanation for a general audience. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The abstract presents an interesting hypothesis and framework, but the technical basis and quantitative claims cannot be evaluated without the full manuscript. I would be supportive if the full paper provides rigorous simulation methodology, robust statistical analysis, and appropriate contextualization of the findings. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that the disulfide bond and β sheet network contribute "unequally" to force transmission is unsupported without statistical analysis and figures. The claim that "localized molecular changes therefore reshape mechanical coupling to the nucleus through distinct routes" is a strong interpretation that requires evidence of distinct mechanisms, not just different quantitative effects. The relevance to laminopathies and HGPS is stated as speculative by the authors, but even the speculative connection lacks a mechanistic rationale in the abstract. The generalization of the "force gate framework" to other mechanically regulated proteins is unsupported. The claim that the work "establishes a framework for dissecting mechanical coupling at protein interfaces under load" is overstated given that no experimental validation is presented and the computational approach is not described in sufficient detail.

Nature-style criteria Shared manuscript claim summary The authors present OpenCGChromatin, a GPU-accelerated coarse-grained chromatin model with residue-level protein and nucleotide-level DNA resolution. They claim it enables near-atomistic simulations of chromatin systems an order of magnitude larger than previously possible, independently predicts linker-length-dependent chromatin structures observed by cryo-ET, resolves histone-tail dynamics inaccessible experimentally, and identifies H4K16 and H3K9 acetylation as the most energetically disruptive modifications for chromatin compaction. They further propose a mechanistic framework positioning chromatin as a semi-flexible stickers-and-spacers polymer whose phase behavior is governed by linker-DNA-imposed nucleosome orientation. Visible evidence base Main text figures 1-8, methods section, and references to supplementary figures 3-17 and tables Missing materials affecting confidence Supplementary Information (model Hamiltonian, parameterization details, validation protocols, full analysis definitions), Source Data files, and Reporting Summary were not provided for review Reviewer Overall assessment This manuscript presents a technically impressive computational advance with the potential to significantly impact the chromatin biology and biomolecular condensate fields. The OpenCGChromatin model addresses a genuine gap: the inability of existing near-atomistic models to access biologically relevant length and time scales. The validation against experimental sedimentation data and cryo-ET structures is a strength, and the mechanistic insights regarding linker-length-dependent phase behavior are conceptually novel. However, several concerns temper my enthusiasm. The central mechanistic claims regarding histone tail accessibility and the energetic dominance of specific acetylation sites rest on analyses whose definitions are only partially visible in the main text. The comparison between 25 bp and 30 bp systems, while informative, conflates linker length with nucleosome repeat length, and the attribution of phase behavior differences to "frustration" versus other physicochemical factors requires more rigorous support. The single-trajectory-per-condition design for the phase separation simulations, acknowledged by the authors, limits statistical confidence in the reported differences. The acetylation study, while suggestive, uses an extreme 50% random acetylation level that may not reflect physiological conditions, and the claim that H4K16 and H3K9 emerge as "most disruptive" requires careful interpretation given the pooling strategy across systems with different acetylation patterns. Overall, the model itself appears to be a valuable community resource, but the biological conclusions, particularly those extending beyond the validated compaction regime, need additional support or more cautious framing. Who would be interested in the results, and why Chromatin biologists studying higher-order genome organization, particularly those interested in the biophysical basis of chromatin phase separation and the role of linker DNA in shaping nuclear architecture. Computational biophysicists developing coarse-grained models of protein-DNA systems will find the methodological advances and GPU implementation of direct interest. Researchers studying histone post-translational modifications, especially acetylation, and their effects on chromatin structure will be interested in the predictive framework for identifying energetically important modification sites. The broader phase separation community, including those studying other nucleic acid-protein systems, may find the stickers-and-spacers framework with explicit spacer mechanics conceptually transferable. Major strengths The model represents a genuine methodological advance, achieving an order-of-magnitude improvement in accessible system size while maintaining near-atomistic resolution. The validation strategy is appropriate: reproducing experimental sedimentation coefficients across linker lengths provides a stringent test, and the agreement with cryo-ET structural features adds confidence. The phase separation predictions are bold and testable, and the connection between single-fiber conformational properties and collective phase behavior is conceptually elegant. The identification of H4K16 and H3K9 as energetically critical acetylation sites from unbiased simulations is a striking result with potential biological significance. The manuscript is generally well-written and the figures are informative. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Statistical rigor and reproducibility Claim pointer The authors claim that 25 bp chromatin phase-separates while 30 bp chromatin shows only weak phase separation, and that 25 bp arrays expand upon phase separation while 30 bp arrays do not. Evidence pointer Figure 4a-d, Figure 5b, Methods section "Phase separation" Concern The phase separation simulations consist of a single trajectory per condition (81 tetranucleosome arrays per simulation, one simulation for 25 bp and one for 30 bp). The authors acknowledge this in the Methods, noting that error bars represent temporal block-to-block variability rather than variation across independent replicates. This design fundamentally limits the statistical confidence in the reported differences between 25 bp and 30 bp systems. The differences in density profiles, largest connected component size, and conformational distributions could reflect initial condition sensitivity or stochastic variation rather than robust thermodynamic differences. The claim that 25 bp chromatin "phase-separates" while 30 bp does not is a strong binary statement resting on n=1 per condition. Why it matters The central mechanistic conclusion of the paper, that linker length controls phase behavior through conformational frustration, depends critically on the reliability of the difference between the 25 bp and 30 bp phase separation simulations. If this difference is not robust across independent simulations, the primary biological claim is undermined. The field of biomolecular condensates is already grappling with reproducibility challenges, and a claim of this significance requires demonstration of robustness. Resolution test The authors should provide at minimum 3 independent simulations per condition (ideally 5 or more) with different random seeds and, if feasible, different initial configurations. The reported differences in density profiles, cluster sizes, and conformational distributions should be shown to be consistent across replicates. Statistical comparison of the 25 bp and 30 bp conditions should be performed using appropriate tests that account for the hierarchical structure of the data (e.g., mixed-effects models or bootstrapping across replicates). Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Claim-evidence alignment Claim pointer The authors claim that "OpenCGChromatin resolves histone-tail dynamics and interaction networks that remain inaccessible experimentally, explaining how linker-DNA length controls histone tail accessibility and the resulting multiscale structure of chromatin condensates." Evidence pointer Figure 6, Methods section "Analysis methods" Concern The energy-weighted contact analysis presented in Figure 6 is central to the mechanistic claim that 30 bp linkers bury H4 and H2A N-terminal tails in intra-array contacts while 25 bp linkers expose all tails for inter-array interactions. However, the definition of the energy-weighted score is only partially described in the main text. The Methods state that contacts are weighted by pairwise interaction energy evaluated at instantaneous separation, but the specific functional form, the treatment of different interaction types (electrostatic vs. Lennard-Jones), and the normalization scheme are not fully specified. The claim that this analysis "resolves" tail dynamics implies a level of detail that may not be supported by the coarse-grained representation. Furthermore, the comparison between intra-array and inter-array contacts in Figure 6a vs 6b is presented as the key mechanistic distinction, but the absolute magnitudes and the statistical significance of the differences between 25 bp and 30 bp conditions are not reported. Why it matters The mechanistic explanation for why linker length controls phase behavior rests on this contact analysis. If the energy-weighted scoring is not rigorously defined and validated, or if the differences between conditions are not statistically robust, the proposed mechanism is not established. The claim of resolving "interaction networks that remain inaccessible experimentally" is strong and requires that the computational analysis be held to a high standard of rigor. Resolution test The authors should provide a complete mathematical definition of the energy-weighted contact score in the main text or clearly reference the Supplementary Information section where it is defined. They should report the statistical significance of the differences between 25 bp and 30 bp conditions for the key contact types (H4, H2A N) in both intra-array and inter-array categories. Ideally, they should also validate the energy-weighted approach against simpler contact frequency analyses to demonstrate that the weighting scheme does not introduce artifacts. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Interpretational overreach Claim pointer The authors state that "the simulations suggest that linker-induced frustration in the 25 bp fibers enables conformational expansion upon phase separation that exposes additional interaction sites, allowing fibers to reorganize and diversify their interaction modes" and that this "provides a direct coupling between single-fiber frustration, histone-tail accessibility, and network connectivity that defines how chromatin's geometry and chemical makeup jointly control its phase behavior." Evidence pointer Figure 5, Figure 6, Discussion Concern The causal chain proposed, from linker length to frustration to expansion to tail exposure to enhanced inter-array connectivity to phase separation, is presented as a coherent mechanism. However, the evidence for each causal link is correlational. The authors show that 25 bp arrays are more expanded in dilute conditions and expand further in the condensed phase, and that tail contacts differ between conditions. But they do not demonstrate that the expansion is caused by frustration rather than by, for example, differences in net charge, hydration, or excluded volume effects. The term "frustration" is used descriptively but is not quantified or directly measured. The claim of a "direct coupling" implies a mechanistic understanding that may exceed what the simulations can establish. Why it matters The conceptual framework presented in the Discussion, positioning chromatin as a semi-flexible stickers-and-spacers polymer where spacer mechanics control phase behavior, is potentially important and generative. However, if the causal claims are overstated relative to the evidence, the framework may be prematurely solidified and could misdirect future research. The distinction between correlation and causation is particularly important in computational studies where the modeler has full access to all variables. Resolution test The authors should either (a) provide additional analyses that directly test the proposed causal chain, such as perturbing specific interactions (e.g., neutralizing specific tail charges, modifying DNA flexibility) and showing the predicted effects on phase behavior, or (b) soften the causal language and present the mechanism as a hypothesis consistent with the simulations rather than a demonstrated principle. Quantifying "frustration" through a measurable order parameter would also strengthen the claim. Concern ID R1-M4 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Generalizability of acetylation findings Claim pointer The authors claim that "extending simulations to 108-nucleosome fibers shows that acetylation disrupts chromatin compaction in a pattern-specific manner by weakening key tail-mediated interactions, with H4K16 and H3K9 emerging as the most energetically disruptive modifications." Evidence pointer Figure 7, Figure 8, Methods section "Long fiber dynamics" Concern The acetylation simulations use a 50% random acetylation level across all lysines in acetylated regions. This is acknowledged as an upper bound, but the interpretation of the results as identifying "the most energetically disruptive modifications" may be sensitive to this choice. The comparison between H4K16 and H3K9 as "most disruptive" is based on a ranking of energy-weighted contact scores, but the statistical significance of this ranking is not established. Furthermore, the simulations use only three acetylation patterns (0 Ac, 5x12 Ac, 54 Ac), and the 5x12 pattern creates alternating blocks of acetylated and unacetylated nucleosomes that may not represent any physiological arrangement. The claim that the findings reveal "pattern-specific" effects is based on a very limited exploration of the pattern space. Why it matters The acetylation results are presented as a key application of the model with potential biological significance. If the conclusions are sensitive to the specific simulation choices (acetylation level, pattern, and the specific lysines modified), the generalizability of the findings is limited. The claim that specific modification sites are "most disruptive" could be misinterpreted as a prediction about which acetylation marks are most biologically important, when the simulations only address which are most disruptive under a specific, extreme acetylation condition. Resolution test The authors should either (a) perform additional simulations with different acetylation levels (e.g., 10%, 25%) and patterns to test the robustness of the ranking, or (b) temper the claims to state that under the specific conditions simulated, H4K16 and H3K9 show the largest energetic effects, without generalizing to biological importance. Reporting confidence intervals or bootstrap estimates for the energy-weighted scores would also help establish the robustness of the ranking. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity of model validation Affected element Figure 2a and Supplementary Figure 4 Evidence pointer Figure 2a, Supplementary Figure 4 Issue The validation against experimental sedimentation coefficients is presented as a key strength, but the figure only shows simulated values with experimental values overlaid. It is unclear how the experimental values were obtained and whether the comparison is apples-to-apples (e.g., same salt conditions, same temperature, same buffer composition). Required correction Please clarify in the figure legend or main text the source of the experimental sedimentation coefficients and any adjustments made to ensure comparability with simulation conditions. If the experimental values are from different buffer conditions, this should be stated and the potential impact on the comparison discussed. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness of benchmarking Affected element Figure 1b Evidence pointer Figure 1b Issue The benchmarking data in Figure 1b are described as single measurements (n=1) with no uncertainty or inferential comparison claimed. While this is appropriate for a hardware benchmark, the claim of "over an order-of-magnitude acceleration" would be more convincing with at least a few repeated measurements to demonstrate stability. Required correction Please provide at least 3 repeated benchmark measurements per condition and report the mean and range, or state clearly that the benchmarks are representative single measurements and the performance gain is approximate. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Statistical reporting Affected element Figure 2b-c, Figure 3a-b, Figure 6, Figure 7d, Figure 8b Evidence pointer Multiple figures Issue The Methods state that error bars represent standard deviations across five temporal blocks from a single trajectory. This is appropriate for describing temporal variability, but the figures do not consistently indicate whether any differences between conditions are statistically significant. For example, in Figure 3a-b, the differences between 10N and 10N+5 contact frequencies appear visually clear, but no statistical test is reported. Required correction Please add statistical comparisons (e.g., t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests on block means) for the key comparisons between conditions, or state explicitly that the reported differences are descriptive and not statistically tested. If the latter, the language in the text should be adjusted to avoid implying statistical significance. Concern ID R1-m4 Severity Minor Axis Parameter sensitivity Affected element Contact definitions Evidence pointer Methods section "Analysis methods" Issue The contact cutoff for residue-residue contacts is defined as rc = 0.5(sigma_i + sigma_j) + 0.25 nm, and the nucleosome-nucleosome contact cutoff is 13 nm. The sensitivity of the results to these choices is not discussed. Given that the central mechanistic claims depend on contact analyses, it would be valuable to know whether the conclusions are robust to reasonable variations in these cutoffs. Required correction Please add a sensitivity analysis in the Supplementary Information showing that the key conclusions (e.g., the ranking of tail contact frequencies, the difference between 25 bp and 30 bp systems) are robust to variations in the contact cutoffs (e.g., +/- 20%). Concern ID R1-m5 Severity Minor Axis Terminology precision Affected element Abstract and Introduction Evidence pointer Abstract, Introduction Issue The term "near-atomistic" is used throughout, but its precise meaning is not defined. The model represents each amino acid as one bead and each nucleotide as one bead, which is a coarse-grained representation, not "near-atomistic" in the sense of retaining atomic detail. The term could be misleading to readers unfamiliar with the field. Required correction Please define "near-atomistic" in the Introduction, clarifying that it refers to residue-level and nucleotide-level resolution, and consider whether a more precise term such as "residue-resolution" or "united-atom" would be more appropriate. Concern ID R1-m6 Severity Minor Axis Discussion of limitations Affected element Discussion Evidence pointer Discussion Issue The Discussion does not adequately address the limitations of the implicit solvent treatment. The Debye-Hückel model is acknowledged in the Methods, but the potential impact of neglecting specific ion effects, hydration forces, and hydrophobic effects on the phase behavior predictions is not discussed. Required correction Please add a paragraph in the Discussion addressing the limitations of the implicit solvent model and how these might affect the quantitative predictions of phase behavior, particularly at the salt concentrations studied. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that OpenCGChromatin "independently predicts" experimental observations is partially supported for sedimentation coefficients but is not established for the phase separation behavior, as the experimental comparison relies on qualitative agreement with prior work from the same group. The claim that H4K16 and H3K9 are "the most energetically disruptive modifications" is not statistically supported and is based on a single simulation per acetylation pattern with an extreme 50% acetylation level. The claim that the model "resolves histone-tail dynamics and interaction networks that remain inaccessible experimentally" is overstated; the model provides predictions that are not directly validated against experimental measurements of tail dynamics. The mechanistic claim of "direct coupling between single-fiber frustration, histone-tail accessibility, and network connectivity" is presented as established but is a hypothesis consistent with the simulations, not a demonstrated causal chain. The claim of "over an order-of-magnitude acceleration" is based on single benchmark measurements and should be treated as approximate. The generalizability of the phase behavior findings to longer, heterogeneous chromatin fibers is acknowledged as limited by the authors, but the Discussion could more prominently caveat this limitation.

manuscript claim summary The authors present Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model derived via transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data from human kidney tissue. They claim accurate cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility prediction, 10–23% improvement in regulatory variant effect prediction over existing models, effective prioritization of kidney function GWAS fine-mapped causal variants with cell-type resolution, sufficiency of a 32–64 kbp local flanking context for variant effect prediction, and comparable performance of a multi-task model at reduced computational cost. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, performance metrics, model architecture details, or validation procedures are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods section, model training and evaluation details, dataset descriptions, baseline model specifications, statistical analyses, and any supplementary information Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a potentially valuable contribution to the field of regulatory genomics by addressing the cell-type specificity gap in existing sequence-to-function models. The transfer learning approach from Borzoi to kidney tissue is conceptually sound and timely. However, the abstract lacks sufficient quantitative detail to evaluate the robustness of the claimed improvements, the validity of the benchmarking procedures, and the generalizability of the findings. The core claims are plausible but currently not verifiable from the provided material. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in regulatory genomics, computational biology, and kidney disease genetics would find these results relevant. Those working on variant effect prediction for clinical interpretation, particularly in the context of kidney function and chronic kidney disease, would benefit from a cell-type-specific model. Additionally, the transfer learning framework and the multi-task efficiency analysis would interest method developers in the deep learning for genomics community. Major strengths The problem addressed is well-defined and important, as existing S2F models lack cell-type specificity. The transfer learning strategy is pragmatic and leverages existing resources. The focus on kidney function GWAS variants provides a clinically relevant application. The ablation analysis of flanking sequence context addresses a practical question about model input requirements. The multi-task efficiency comparison is a useful practical consideration. 01 基本信息 标题 ：From reference-genome prediction to causal generalization: sequence-to-function models for plant regulatory genomics 作者 ：Zhan, Mingfang; Wu, Ruigang 单位 ：未提供 期刊/平台 ：Frontiers in Plant Science 年份 ：2026-10-02 论文类型 ：Mini Review（迷你综述） 领域 ：植物调控基因组学 × 序列-功能（seq2func）深度学习模型 关键词 ：sequence-to-function models, plant regulatory genomics, pan-genome, causal generalization, distribution shift, closed-loop AI（基于全文归纳） DOI/ID ：10.3389/fpls.2026.1968878 URL ：https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42824471/ 代码 ：未提供 数据 ：未提供 阅读日期 ：未提供 在「三维基因组/染色质组织 × AI 方法/物理模拟」方向中的位置 ：本文不直接研究三维基因组或染色质高级结构，而是聚焦植物调控基因组学中的序列-功能预测模型。但其核心关切——从参考基因组观测数据到跨基因型/环境/物种的因果泛化——与三维基因组领域面临的泛化挑战高度同构。文中讨论的分布偏移（distribution shift）评估框架、观测与扰动实验互补、主动学习与持续学习闭环等思路，可直接迁移到染色质构象预测模型的评估与迭代设计中。文中提及的染色质互作信息作为预测基因表达的输入特征（如DeepCBA），也构成与三维基因组方法的直接接口。 02 一句话总结 本文是一篇迷你综述，系统梳理植物调控基因组学中序列-功能（seq2func）模型的现状与局限，指出基于参考基因组的观测数据训练与评估无法保证对自然单倍型、结构变异、组织、发育阶段、环境及物种的泛化，并提出以生物学有意义的分布偏移为基准的评估框架，以及结合泛基因组、多组学、基因组编辑、报告基因检测、主动学习和持续学习的闭环实验-计算系统作为改进路径。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：seq2func 模型在植物调控基因组学中，从参考基因组预测到跨遗传/环境/物种的因果泛化，面临哪些挑战？如何评估和改进其泛化能力？ 为什么重要 ：植物基因组具有高重复序列含量、转座子丰富、多倍化普遍、长程调控广泛、基因型-环境互作（G×E）复杂等特点。若模型仅在参考基因组上表现良好，则无法有效应用于育种群体中的非参考等位基因、结构变异或工程化调控序列，限制了其在精准育种和气候韧性作物改良中的实际价值。 现有方法为何不足 ：当前大多数模型在单一或少数参考基因组的观测数据上训练和评估，随机留出位点的测试仅衡量熟悉环境中的插值能力，而非对植物生物学和育种最相关的变异类型的预测能力。观测关联不能确立因果关系，高留出准确率不等于模型恢复了真实的调控规则。 精确的「Can ... ?」研究问题 ：Can sequence-to-function models trained on reference-genome observational data generalize reliably to non-reference haplotypes, structural variants, tissues, environments, and species in plants, and can their predictions be validated as causal through perturbation assays? 04 背景与发展脉络 注：以下脉络主要基于本文框架构建，标注「仅本文框架」；部分外部引用经文中提及，标注「经外部核验（文中引用）」。 阶段 代表性方法/事件 优点 局限 本文主张的位置 早期 seq2func 奠基 Zhou and Troyanskaya (2015); Kelley et al. 节） 06 核心思想 1) 表面方法 本文是一篇迷你综述，不提出新模型，而是系统性地： - 梳理植物 seq2func 模型的现状（CNN、Transformer/长上下文架构、基因组语言模型）； - 列举植物基因组对 seq2func 的独特挑战（泛基因组多样性、转座子、多倍体、远端调控、上下文依赖）； - 提出以分布偏移（covariate shift / label shift / concept shift）为分类框架的评估基准； - 提出观测（多组学）+ 扰动（MPRA/STARR-seq/CRISPR 编辑）互补的因果验证路径； - 提出主动学习 + 持续学习 + 闭环实验-计算系统的迭代框架。 2) 核心洞察 泛化不是插值 ：参考基因组上的随机留出测试衡量的是熟悉环境中的插值能力，而植物育种和调控发现真正需要的是对非参考等位基因、结构变异、新环境和新物种的外推能力。 三种分布偏移的区分 ：将评估问题分解为 covariate shift（序列分布变化）、label shift（测量过程变化）、concept shift（序列-功能映射关系变化），为设计有意义的基准提供了可操作框架。 观测与扰动的互补性 ：观测数据（ATAC-seq、ChIP-seq、RNA-seq）提供内源染色质环境中的关联证据，报告基因检测提供分离的序列内在活性，内源编辑提供因果验证——三者构成从关联到因果的证据链。 闭环而非一次性预测 ：模型不应是静态注释工具，而应作为"虚拟实验"参与迭代——不确定性指导实验选择，实验结果反馈更新模型。 3) 可能的普适教训 [Analysis] 评估协议决定结论边界 ：任何序列-功能（或序列-结构）预测模型的性能声明都必须限定其训练数据覆盖的序列空间和生物学上下文。对三维基因组模型而言，这意味着跨细胞类型、跨物种、跨构象状态的评估应成为标准实践。 "上下文"是模型的核心变量而非噪声 ：植物中组织/环境/发育对调控的影响提示，染色质结构预测模型同样需要显式编码细胞状态和实验条件，而非仅依赖序列。 因果验证是模型可信度的最终标尺 ：预测染色质互作或调控效应的模型，其价值最终取决于能否通过扰动实验（如 CRISPR 删除增强子、染色质构象捕获后的编辑验证）得到确认。 07 方法总览 本文为综述，无原始方法。但文中提出的闭环框架可概括为： 输入 ：参考基因组与泛基因组序列、多组学观测数据（ATAC-seq、DNase-seq、ChIP-seq、CUT&Tag、RNA-seq、 nascent transcription、染色体构象数据）、报告基因检测数据（MPRA、STARR-seq）、内源编辑结果（CRISPR 删除/替换/碱基编辑/CRISPRi/a） 输出 ：调控元件注释、变异效应预测、序列设计建议、经实验验证的因果调控机制 核心模块 ： 1. seq2func 预测模型 ：CNN 基线、长上下文 Transformer/状态空间架构、基因组语言模型 2. 分布偏移评估框架 ：covariate shift（新单倍型/结构变异/物种）、label shift（不同检测平台/测量类型）、concept shift（不同组织/发育/环境） 3. 扰动实验模块 ：MPRA/STARR-seq 高通量报告基因检测 + CRISPR 内源编辑验证 4. 主动学习模块 ：基于模型不确定性（高不确定性、模型分歧、 underrepresented haplotypes）选择下一轮实验 5. 持续学习模块 ：replay-based rehearsal、参数正则化（EWC）、模块化 adapter 架构，避免灾难性遗忘 流程 ：观测数据训练模型 → 在分布偏移基准上评估 → 不确定性指导选择扰动实验 → 实验结果验证/修正预测 → 持续学习更新模型 → 循环迭代 08 核心模块拆解 模块 功能 为何需要 输入输出 支撑证据 Scientific content, technical soundness, clarity, and alignment with stated scope; no assessment of editorial fit or publication policy Shared manuscript claim summary The manuscript argues that sequence-to-function (seq2func) models in plant regulatory genomics, while improving in accuracy, are predominantly trained and evaluated on observational data from reference genomes, and therefore may not generalize to natural genetic, developmental, environmental, or species diversity. It proposes evaluation frameworks based on biologically meaningful distribution shifts and outlines a closed-loop experimental–computational system involving pan-genomes, multi-omics, genome editing, reporter assays, active learning, and continual learning. Visible evidence base Full text including abstract, introduction, sections on seq2func models, plant-specific challenges, causal inference, evaluation frameworks, and closed-loop systems; one figure referenced (Figure 1); one table referenced (Table 1); citations to prior work Missing materials affecting confidence Figure 1 and Table 1 are referenced but not provided; no data, code, or empirical results are included; no supplementary materials; no line numbers Reviewer Overall assessment This Mini Review provides a well-structured and timely synthesis of seq2func modelling in plant regulatory genomics, with a clear emphasis on generalization beyond reference genomes. The manuscript is conceptually coherent and identifies important gaps in current evaluation practices. However, several claims are made without direct evidence or detailed support, and the absence of Figure 1 and Table 1 limits full assessment. The review would benefit from more concrete examples, quantitative benchmarks, and a clearer distinction between established findings and proposed directions. Who would be interested in the results, and why Researchers in plant functional genomics, computational biology, and breeding, particularly those working on cis-regulatory element discovery, variant effect prediction, and integration of multi-omics data. The manuscript is also relevant to method developers in machine learning applied to genomics, and to those interested in causal inference and experimental design in plant systems. Major strengths The manuscript addresses a timely and important problem: the gap between reference-genome-based prediction and real-world genetic and environmental diversity in plants. The discussion of distribution shifts (covariate, label, concept) is a useful framework. The emphasis on combining observational and perturbation data, and on closed-loop systems, is forward-looking and practical. The writing is clear and accessible for a broad audience. Major Concerns Several claims are made without supporting data or detailed examples. The manuscript repeatedly states that models may not generalize, but does not provide quantitative evidence or case studies. The discussion of polyploidy and transposable elements is general and lacks specific examples of model failures. The proposed evaluation frameworks are described at a high level but not operationalized. The absence of Figure 1 and Table 1 prevents assessment of key illustrative content. Some statements are repeated verbatim (e.g., the sentence about interpretability methods), suggesting incomplete editing. Minor Comments The manuscript would benefit from a glossary of terms for nonspecialists. Some references are cited but not discussed in context. The section on closed-loop systems is speculative and could be strengthened by referencing existing examples in other fields. The conclusion is somewhat repetitive of earlier sections. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established The manuscript does not provide empirical evidence or detailed case studies to support the central claim that seq2func models fail to generalize. The proposed evaluation frameworks are not tested or exemplified. The absence of Figure 1 and Table 1 means that key content cannot be evaluated. Some claims about model limitations are stated as fact without citation or data. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The manuscript offers a useful synthesis but does not present novel methods or data; the conceptual framework of distribution shifts is not new but is applied here to plant genomics in a coherent way. Scientific importance: The topic is important and timely, but the manuscript does not provide new evidence or a testable framework that would advance the field beyond current discussions. Interdisciplinary readership: The manuscript is accessible to a broad audience, but the lack of concrete examples and data may limit its impact. Technical soundness: The manuscript is technically sound in its descriptions but lacks empirical support for its central claims. Readability for nonspecialists: The writing is clear, but some sections assume familiarity with machine learning and genomics terminology. Recommendation posture Supportive if technical concerns are resolved, particularly the addition of concrete examples, quantitative benchmarks, and the inclusion of Figure 1 and Table 1. Currently, the manuscript is a reasonable review but does not establish a strong case for its central claims from the provided evidence. methods, or supplementary materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors propose that a subset of T1D-associated genetic variants disrupt transcription factor binding at cell type-specific candidate cis-regulatory elements in human pancreatic islets, thereby altering gene expression and contributing to β-cell dysfunction. They integrate public epigenomic and single-cell multiomic datasets with T1D GWAS variants, apply ChromBPNet to predict variant effects on chromatin accessibility, and use TF footprinting to nominate transcription factors. They report identification of several T1D-associated SNPs predicted to alter chromatin accessibility at candidate TF binding sites. Visible evidence base Abstract text only; no quantitative results, validation metrics, or dataset identifiers beyond PANC-DB and ChromBPNet are provided Missing materials affecting confidence Full manuscript, all figures and tables, methods details, model training and evaluation procedures, variant lists, statistical thresholds, and any validation experiments Reviewer Overall assessment The abstract presents a plausible and potentially valuable analytical framework for linking T1D-associated noncoding variants to cell type-specific regulatory effects in pancreatic islets. The integration of public epigenomic data with GWAS variants and deep learning-based accessibility prediction is methodologically current. However, the abstract provides no quantitative evidence, no validation of predictions, and no demonstration that the identified variants have functional consequences. The core claim that specific SNPs "may contribute to β-cell dysfunction" remains speculative and is not supported by the evidence presented in the abstract. The work is at a hypothesis-generating stage and would require substantial additional evidence to establish a mechanistic case. Who would be interested in the results, and why Geneticists and epigenomics researchers studying autoimmune disease risk variants, particularly those focused on type 1 diabetes and pancreatic islet biology. Investigators working on the functional interpretation of noncoding GWAS variants and those developing computational pipelines for variant effect prediction would also find the approach relevant. The potential link between β-cell-intrinsic regulatory variation and T1D pathogenesis could interest the broader diabetes research community. Major strengths The study addresses an important gap in understanding how T1D-associated variants may act through β-cell-intrinsic mechanisms. The integration of multiple public datasets, including single-cell multiomic data, is appropriate for the question. The use of ChromBPNet for base-pair-resolution prediction is a current and technically suitable approach. The focus on cell type-specific regulatory programs is well motivated by the biology of T1D. Major Concerns Concern ID R1-M1 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Evidence sufficiency Claim pointer The authors claim that "several T1D-associated SNPs predicted to alter chromatin accessibility at candidate TF binding sites" were identified, and that these findings "link T1D-associated variants to cell type-specific enhancer activity and regulatory pathways." Evidence pointer Abstract only; no figures or tables provided Concern The abstract reports the identification of SNPs predicted to alter chromatin accessibility but provides no quantitative information. No number of variants identified, no effect sizes, no statistical significance thresholds, no comparison to control variants, and no assessment of prediction confidence are given. Without these data, the reader cannot evaluate whether the findings exceed what would be expected by chance or whether the predictions are biologically meaningful. Why it matters The central claim of the paper rests on the identification of specific variants with predicted regulatory effects. If the predictions are not benchmarked against known functional variants or validated experimentally, the results may represent false positives from a computational pipeline. The absence of any quantitative evidence prevents assessment of the robustness and specificity of the findings. Resolution test Provide the number of T1D-associated SNPs tested, the number predicted to alter accessibility, the distribution of predicted effect sizes, and a comparison against matched control variants. Include validation metrics for ChromBPNet performance on islet data and, ideally, experimental validation of at least one or two top candidate variants. Concern ID R1-M2 Severity Major Blocking Yes Axis Functional validation Claim pointer The authors state that their findings "suggest mechanisms by which noncoding variants may contribute to β-cell dysfunction and T1D susceptibility." Evidence pointer Abstract only; no experimental data described Concern The abstract describes only computational predictions. No experimental evidence is presented to show that any identified variant actually alters TF binding, chromatin accessibility, or gene expression in relevant cell types. The leap from predicted regulatory effects to a claim about contribution to β-cell dysfunction is not supported by the evidence described. Why it matters Computational predictions of variant effects on regulatory elements are known to have substantial false positive rates. Without experimental validation, such as reporter assays, electrophoretic mobility shift assays, or CRISPR-based perturbation in stem cell-derived β cells or islet models, the biological relevance of the identified variants remains unestablished. The claim of a mechanistic link is therefore premature. Resolution test Include experimental validation for at least a subset of top candidate variants demonstrating allele-specific effects on TF binding, enhancer activity, or gene expression in a relevant cellular context. Alternatively, provide strong orthogonal evidence such as allele-specific accessibility or expression quantitative trait loci data from primary human islets. Concern ID R1-M3 Severity Major Blocking No Axis Methodological transparency Claim pointer The authors state that they "integrated publicly available epigenomic datasets" and "combined these data with T1D GWAS variants to identify disease-associated SNPs located within enhancer regions." Evidence pointer Abstract only; dataset identifiers and analysis details not provided Concern The abstract does not specify which GWAS dataset was used, how linkage disequilibrium was handled, which epigenomic marks defined enhancers, how cell type-specific cCREs were called, or how the multiomic datasets from PANC-DB were processed. The criteria for selecting candidate variants for ChromBPNet analysis are not described. Why it matters The reproducibility and validity of the findings depend critically on these methodological choices. Different GWAS datasets, LD thresholds, and enhancer definitions could substantially change the set of candidate variants identified. Without this information, the results cannot be evaluated or reproduced. Resolution test Provide a detailed methods section specifying all data sources, quality control procedures, analysis parameters, and thresholds. Include a flowchart or schematic of the analytical pipeline. Minor Comments Concern ID R1-m1 Severity Minor Axis Clarity Affected element Terminology Evidence pointer Abstract, first paragraph Issue The phrase "candidate cis-regulatory elements (cCREs)" is used without defining the criteria for what constitutes a "candidate" element in this context. Required correction Define cCREs explicitly, including the epigenomic marks and thresholds used to call them. Concern ID R1-m2 Severity Minor Axis Completeness Affected element TF nomination Evidence pointer Abstract, methods description Issue The abstract states that TF footprinting was used to "nominate TFs likely to bind these variant-containing regions" but does not indicate whether the nominated TFs are known to be expressed in the relevant islet cell types. Required correction State whether TF expression in the relevant cell types was confirmed using the available single-cell data. Concern ID R1-m3 Severity Minor Axis Interpretation Affected element Causal direction Evidence pointer Abstract, final sentence Issue The abstract implies that altered chromatin accessibility at variant sites would lead to β-cell dysfunction, but the direction of causality is not established. Altered accessibility could be a consequence of disease state rather than a cause. Required correction Acknowledge the correlational nature of the findings and discuss the possibility that accessibility changes reflect rather than drive disease processes. Technical failings that need to be addressed before the case is established R1-M1 and R1-M2 are the primary technical concerns. The absence of quantitative results and the lack of any experimental or orthogonal validation mean that the central claims of the paper are not currently supported. R1-M3 regarding methodological transparency must also be addressed to allow evaluation of the analytical approach. Assessment against Nature-style criteria Originality: The combination of public epigenomic integration, single-cell multiomic analysis, and deep learning-based variant effect prediction applied specifically to T1D islets has elements of novelty, though each individual component is established in the field. Scientific importance: The question of how T1D risk variants act through β-cell-intrinsic mechanisms is important and timely. If the findings are robust, they could inform understanding of disease pathogenesis. Interdisciplinary readership: The work would appeal to geneticists, epigenomics researchers, and diabetes biologists, but the abstract as written is unlikely to attract a broader readership without clearer articulation of biological significance. Technical soundness: Cannot be assessed from the abstract alone. The absence of quantitative results and validation is a major limitation. Readability for nonspecialists: The abstract is reasonably clear but uses specialized terminology without sufficient context. The logical flow from hypothesis to methods to findings is understandable. Recommendation posture Currently not established from the provided evidence. The analytical framework is promising and the question is important, but the abstract provides no quantitative support for the central claims and no validation of the computational predictions. The manuscript would need to include detailed results, benchmarking, and ideally experimental validation before the case for a mechanistic link between T1D variants and β-cell dysfunction can be considered. Risk / unsupported claims The claim that "several T1D-associated SNPs predicted to alter chromatin accessibility at candidate TF binding sites" were identified is unsupported because no quantitative results are provided. The claim that the findings "suggest mechanisms by which noncoding variants may contribute to β-cell dysfunction" is unsupported because no functional validation or causal evidence is presented. The claim that the identified variants "link T1D-associated variants to cell type-specific enhancer activity and regulatory pathways" is not evaluable without details on the enhancer definitions and variant selection criteria. The overall hypothesis that T1D-associated variants directly influence cCREs by disrupting TF binding is plausible but remains unverified by the evidence described in the abstract.

materials were provided Shared manuscript claim summary The authors introduce EpiZoo, a 2.6 billion parameter mixture-of-experts transformer foundation model for cross-species single-cell epigenomics. The model converts single-cell epigenomic profiles into "cell sentences" integrating DNA sequence information, sequence-independent epigenomic context, and accessibility-based importance. 01 基本信息 标题 ：Deep Learning Predicts Hematopoietic Stem Cell Aging From 3D Chromatin Images 作者 ：Picazo, Pablo Ianez; Mejia-Ramirez, Eva; Di Bari, Dario; Vitali, Elena; Florian, Maria Carolina; Petrone, Paula 单位 ：未提供（从致谢推断涉及 ISGlobal Biomedical Data Science 与 IDIBELL Stem Cell Aging lab） 期刊/预印本平台 ：Aging Cell 年份 ：2026-09-28 论文类型 ：研究论文（Research Article） 领域 ：三维基因组 / 染色质组织 × AI / 干细胞衰老 关键词 ：chromatin architecture, deep learning, CNN, hematopoietic stem cell aging, explainable AI, drug screening DOI/arXiv 号 ：10.1111/acel.70656 代码 ：https://github.com/biomedical-data-science/chromagenet 数据 ：https://doi.org/10.34810/data2372（CORA 仓库） 阅读日期 ：未提供 在课题方向中的位置 ：本文属于「三维基因组/染色质组织 × AI 方法」方向中基于 3D 显微镜图像（而非 Hi-C/3C 数据）的染色质结构表型预测模型。其核心贡献在于：(1) 将 CNN 应用于 DAPI 染色的 3D 核图像进行衰老分类；(2) 通过 XAI 提取可解释的染色质空间特征；(3) 展示作为药物筛选表型读出的潜力。与 Hi-C 驱动的 3D 基因组预测模型互补，提供了一条基于成像的染色质组织量化路径。 02 一句话总结 本文构建了一个基于 CNN 的可解释深度学习框架 ChromAgeNet，以 DAPI 染色的 3D 共聚焦显微镜图像为输入，区分年轻与衰老小鼠造血干细胞（HSC），在核水平达到 AUROC 0.77 ± 0.03，优于基于手工染色质特征的经典机器学习模型，并通过 XAI 识别出染色质熵、外周异染色质和染色质凝聚体作为预测标志物。 03 研究问题 具体问题 ：3D 染色质结构图像中是否编码了足以区分年轻与衰老 HSC 的信息？能否用深度学习自动提取这些信息并做出可靠预测？ 为什么重要 ：造血系统衰老影响机体功能与健康寿命，HSC 功能衰退是核心驱动因素。目前缺乏能够量化单细胞水平年龄相关染色质状态的方法。若能从染色质图像预测生物学年龄，将有助于衰老机制研究、 rejuvenation 疗法评估和高通量药物筛选。 现有方法为何不足 ：(1) 基于 DNA 甲基化的表观遗传时钟需要分子生物学实验，成本高、通量低；(2) 手工提取的染色质特征（radiomics）需要预定义特征集，可能遗漏关键信息；(3) 此前尚无工作将深度学习直接应用于 3D 染色质图像预测 HSC 衰老。 精确研究问题 ：Can a CNN trained on 3D DAPI-stained chromatin images of HSC nuclei distinguish young from aged murine HSCs with higher accuracy than classical ML models trained on handcrafted chromatin features, and can XAI reveal interpretable chromatin patterns underlying the predictions?
